stage_a.note: Clear positive engagement and smiling while introducing the product.
Sustained engagement describing the ingredients and flavors.
Friendly, approachable, playful interaction about drinking options.

venture.description: A non-alcoholic apéritif meant to be mixed into spritzes or consumed as a ready-to-drink beverage.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces herself, her background, and pitches Ghia, explaining its purpose and ingredients.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks how to drink the product and requests to try it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 agrees and wants to have a drink together with the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees to have a drink with the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 demonstrates the different ready-made spritzes and mixes available for the panel to taste.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 praises the taste of the drink.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks about the calorie count of the drink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that it has about 50 calories.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 clarifies if she means 50 calories in the whole can.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms it is 50 calories for the whole can.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reiterates that he loves the taste of the drink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the drink is akin to an Italian amaro or Campari.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 agrees it reminds him of a Campari.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees with S4's comparison.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 adds that it is an all-natural and lighter version.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 praises the taste in French.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S5 in French.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 notes that the drink contains bitters.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 also praises the taste in French.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks for the retail price and the cost to make each unit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 details the retail prices and manufacturing costs for both the bottle and the spritz.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 prompts F1 to discuss the business and sales numbers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shares that they made $2.5 million in their first calendar year, mostly online.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1, S3, and S5 react with surprise and praise to the sales figures.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how they sold that much and if they were profitable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they launched with an Instagram post that took off.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 repeats his question about whether they made money on the $2.5 million sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers they are not profitable yet due to heavy investments.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how much money the business lost last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they lost a little under a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how much capital they put into the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 deflects by stating they have a million dollars worth of inventory.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 clarifies the question, asking how much money they have raised.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they raised $3.5 million and are currently raising another $6.5 million.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the valuation of the $3.5 million round.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the first $900k was raised on a SAFE at a $7.5 million valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 clarifies if the first $900k was raised pre-revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms and lists the high-profile companies she previously worked for.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how much equity F1 still owns.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states she will own 57% after the current $6.5 million round.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the valuation of the current $6.5 million round.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states it is a $35 million pre-money valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 calculates the post-money valuation to be $41 million.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the projected sales for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 projects $4.5 million in sales, doubling the following year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokes that he needs an alcoholic drink after hearing the valuation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 challenges the $5 million valuation offered to the Sharks compared to the $40 million external valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the equity offered to the Sharks comes directly from her personal shares.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 commends F1 for using her own shares.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains she wants a Shark's help to build a huge business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 highlights her hustle, mentioning she personally reached out to hundreds of accounts on Instagram.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 praises F1's hustle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 continues pitching her vision that non-alcoholic drinks are the future of restaurant menus.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 exits because his acid reflux prevents him from drinking the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S1 for his time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits because she cannot consume citrus or bitter things due to a similar condition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S2.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, stating the beverage category is too difficult and expensive to scale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S3.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 agrees with S3 about the category's difficulty but praises F1's success.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 offers exactly what F1 asked for: $250k for 5%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 interrupts, suggesting F1 should hear an offer from someone in the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 argues that S5 is in the wine business, not non-alcoholic drinks.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 if she wants to hear his offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 warns F1 she is about to get a second offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 states he won't negotiate against others and threatens to step out if she listens to S5.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states it wouldn't be fair not to hear everyone out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 agrees that F1's stance is reasonable.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 withdraws his offer and exits the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 expresses disappointment at S4's withdrawal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 challenges F1, asking why she came to the Tank if she wouldn't take an exact offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 explains he withdrew because she wanted to hear more after he gave her exactly what she wanted.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S4.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 states his offer won't change despite the drama, emphasizing his value in the space.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 offers $250k for 10% equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 points out that F1's valuation just got crushed by S5's offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 justifies his higher equity ask by saying he has to work on the business.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 reiterates his brand value as Chef Wonderful and Mr. Wonderful.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 accuses S5 of costing F1 a deal with S4.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 dismisses S1, reminding him he is already out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks F1 for her thoughts on S5's offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 rejects S5's offer, stating it would be unfair to her early supporters.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 argues she has 57% and can do what she wants, standing firm on 10%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reiterates her rejection of S5's offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 commends F1 for standing her ground.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks the panel and leaves.

decisions.note: Has acid reflux, cannot drink it.
Cannot eat citrus or bitter things, affects her.
Category is too hard and expensive to scale.
Matches the ask exactly, believes she is killing it in a hard category.
Does not want to wait while she hears other offers after he gave exactly what she asked for.
Exits the deal along with withdrawing his offer.
Wants more equity for his value and the difficulty of the business.

decisions.terms: I'm not in a position to accept an offer like that...
decisions.note: Cannot accept without doing wrong to early supporters.

record.notes: Standard pitch flow. S4 withdraws his offer and exits simultaneously.
